title: Split a scored tablet in a pill cutter and put one half in each of two medicine cups
instruction: Split this scored tablet in half with the pill cutter, then put one half in each of the two medicine cups.
context: Many prescriptions are half tablets. Pharmacy technicians (SOC 29-2052, about 0.46M) split scored tablets when packing unit-dose cards, and nursing assistants (SOC 31-1131, about 1.4M) split them at a care-home med cart. A technician or aide lays a scored tablet in the V cradle of a pill cutter, shuts the lid so the blade splits it along the score line, opens the lid again and sets the two halves out for two doses, here one in each of two medicine cups. The cutter is a few grams of plastic with a hinged lid, the tablet is a caplet under 2 g, and the halves are small, so the work needs a careful pinch, a tablet seated at the blade and a lid that is really shut and then really opened.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A typical pill splitter (80 x 40 mm base 11 mm tall with a 20 mm wide V cradle running left-right, fixed to the table by its feet; a 30 g splitter in all, its hinged lid (12 g) with a blade over the cradle's middle and a 24 mm tall, 6 mm thick pull fin standing on it near its free edge) stands at x 0.36, y 0.21 with its hinge on the robot's side. The lid starts open at 95 degrees (past upright, against its stop, so it stays open on its own). One scored white caplet (20 x 9 x 7.5 mm, 1.8 g) lies in a pill dish at x 0.28, y 0.33, its length left-right. A dosing tray with two 30 mL medicine cups (38 mm inside, 30 mm tall, one orange, one blue, 60 mm apart left-right) stands at x 0.30, y 0.44.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each. (1) The caplet lies in the V cradle at the blade (its middle within 2.5 mm of the blade and the cradle's line, length along the cradle within 8 degrees, level within 8 degrees); once reached. (2) The lid has been shut (within 3 degrees) on it there, which cuts it: once reached. (3) The lid is open again, past 80 degrees, as things stand. (4) After the cut, one half is in the orange cup and the other in the blue cup (each inside the cup's wall and below its rim), and no gripper pad is within 3 cm of either half or of the lid's fin. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once every full-success condition has held together, without a break, for 1 s: all four steps, and the caplet halves within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where they were when that second began; any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8, also while it is being timed. 0 overall if the caplet or a half falls off the table. Closing the lid on an empty cradle or on a badly seated caplet cuts nothing. The cut is declared at the lid within 3 degrees with the caplet seated; the sim does not check the blade force (real 5.6-22.2 N applied at the fin and 12-48 N at the pill, measured on a standard hand pill cutter, UW-Madison BME Table 1; see fidelity).
reset_notes: Open the lid to its 95 degree stop, lay the caplet in the dish pocket with its length left-right, and stand the tray on its spot.
fidelity: 240/20 Hz. True size: splitter 80x40 mm (95 deg lid, 0.6 N m s/rad), caplet 20x9x7.5 mm 1.8 g. Caplet/halves 1 mm squeeze (2.5 N/finger; 20 N ejected it), pad tips 4.1 mm above underside; fin 8 mm squeeze (14-15 N/finger). Blade 16x0.8x18 mm: collider upper 7 mm above caplet, lower 11 mm cutting edge. Cut declared at lid <=3 deg with caplet seated; measured real force 5.6-22.2 N at handle, 12-48 N at pill (UW-Madison BME, RERC Table 1); demo fin 14-15 N matches; sim: lid angle only.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 at step 1,889 (2,400-step Dream run was pool_full with no actions; Isaac and MuJoCo demos 1.0 at step 1,889)
